prompt: Why keep configuration in a ConfigMap rather than in the image?
hint: Think of the test cluster and production.

choices.text: So one image runs everywhere
choices.why: Right. The image is tested once and each cluster holds its own ConfigMap.

choices.text: Because ConfigMaps are encrypted and images are not
choices.why: A ConfigMap is plain text in etcd; secrets are lesson 14.

choices.text: Because an image cannot read environment variables
choices.why: A program in an image reads variables as anywhere else.

choices.text: So the configuration can be larger than the image
choices.why: A ConfigMap is limited to one mebibyte.

prompt: `kubectl get configmaps` listed `kube-root-ca.crt`, which Ana never created. What is it?

choices.text: A leftover from the cluster's installation that can be deleted
choices.why: The cluster puts it there on purpose, in every namespace, and puts it back.

choices.text: The certificate pods use to check they are talking to the real API server
choices.why: Right. It holds the cluster's CA, so a pod can verify the server it calls.

choices.text: The shop's TLS certificate
choices.why: The shop serves plain HTTP here; this belongs to the cluster.

choices.text: A ConfigMap kind makes for its own nodes
choices.why: Every Kubernetes cluster makes it, kind or not.

prompt: The volume mounts the ConfigMap `shop-files` at `/etc/shop`. Which file does the container find there?

choices.text: `/etc/shop/greeting.txt`, the name of the original file
choices.why: The key was named `greeting` in `--from-file=greeting=greeting.txt`, and keys name the files.

choices.text: `/etc/shop/shop-files`, named after the ConfigMap
choices.why: The ConfigMap's name names the volume source, not a file.

choices.text: `/etc/shop/greeting`
choices.why: Right: the key `greeting` became a file of that name.

choices.text: Nothing until the pod restarts
choices.why: The shop read the file on its first request.

prompt: Ana changed both ConfigMaps. About 86 seconds later, what did the running shop report?
hint: One of the two is copied into the process when it starts.

choices.text: Both values changed
choices.why: The variable still said `Ana's shop`.

choices.text: Neither changed until the pod was deleted
choices.why: The file changed with no restart at all.

choices.text: The variable changed and the file did not
choices.why: It is the other way round.

choices.text: The new file, with the old variable
choices.why: Right. The kubelet refreshed the mounted file; an environment variable never changes in a running process.

prompt: What made the shop finally report `GREETING=Ana's new shop`?
hint: A new container read the variable.

choices.text: Waiting a second minute for the kubelet
choices.why: The kubelet refreshes files, never a process's environment.

choices.text: `kubectl rollout restart`, which replaced the pod
choices.why: Right. The replacement started with the ConfigMap's current value.

choices.text: Applying the ConfigMap a second time
choices.why: It was already applied; the running process was the problem.

choices.text: Marking the ConfigMap immutable
choices.why: That stops changes; it does not deliver them.

prompt: A team stores feature flags in a ConfigMap, read as environment variables. They flip a flag in an emergency and nothing changes for ten minutes. What is the most accurate diagnosis?
hint: How long would they have waited with a file?

choices.text: The kubelet is slow; it should refresh within a minute
choices.why: That delay is about mounted files; variables are never refreshed.

choices.text: The ConfigMap was immutable
choices.why: Then the edit itself would have been refused.

choices.text: Nothing will change until the pods are replaced
choices.why: Right. A variable is fixed at start; a rollout, or flags read from a file the program rereads, is what works.

choices.text: The flag reached half the pods and needs a Service to reach the rest
choices.why: Services route requests, not configuration; and no running pod got it.

prompt: A ConfigMap with `___: true` refuses every edit to its data; changing it means creating a new one.
hint: The API server's error named the field.

prompt: Match each piece of configuration with the better way to deliver it.

pairs.left: The currency the shop prices in

pairs.right: A file on a configMap volume

pairs.left: Prices for one month, never edited

right_distractors: A new image for every change
